What does HTTP status code 418 mean?

events.reply:
HTTP status code 418 means "I'm a teapot."

It originated as an April Fools' joke in RFC 2324 (1998), the "Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol" (HTCPCP). The spec says that any attempt to brew coffee with a teapot should result in the error code "418 I'm a teapot," and that the resulting entity body "may be short and stout."

It was never intended as a serious part of HTTP, but it became a running joke among developers and has been implemented in many web frameworks and libraries as an Easter egg. In 2017 there was a proposal to remove it from software, which prompted a community effort to "Save 418," and RFC 7168 later extended HTCPCP to teapots, formally reserving the code. The IETF's official HTTP status code registry lists 418 as "Unused" with a note that it is reserved due to its use as an April Fools' joke.
